page0.text: Night has come, and it's time to make a decision.

page1.text:
We aren't going out on patrol.
Tohsaka's totally exhausted after spending the entire day making a mold of the Jeweled Sword. She's resting in her room.
The same goes for Illya.
After the three of us ate dinner in silence, we went off to our respective bedrooms.

page2.text:
It's 10 o'clock at night.
...If history is any indication, the Shadow should be moving soon.

page3.text:
...
I stand up without making any noise.
I pick up a knife from the kitchen counter and leave the room.

page4.text:
The door isn't locked.
I quietly open it and walk up to the bed.

page5.text:
...
Sakura is sleeping.
That's all I know.
I can't tell just by looking if her condition has improved or worsened.

page6.text:
Something's wrong with my eyesight.
Sakura's sleeping right in front of me, but I can't tell what face she's making.

page7.text:
"Gh..."
I fight down my dizziness and shaking.
Make up your mind.
Even as I stand here, the Shadow might be attacking people in town right now.

page8.text:
The most direct way to defeat it is to  Sakura right now.
Even if it isn't her fault, someone else will get hurt unless I do it.
People could die.
Innocent people, unable to resist.
...Even Sakura, who never asked to commit these sins.

page9.text:
"..."
I raise the knife.
My mouth is dry.
My tongue feels like cardboard.
The blade is cold and unfeeling.

page10.text:
When I imagine this thin strip of metal, which only exists to be sharp, plunging into the soft flesh of Sakura's living human throat, my eyes go numb.
Like the feeling of falling onto a flathead screwdriver that happened to be bouncing up and stabs me directly in one of my eyeballs.
The numb pain of going blind rips the meninges off of my brain like when someone removes the peel off an orange.

page11.text:
...
My senses are going haywire.
The fingers that are gripping the knife look like they're being bent backwards by an unseen force.
Like telekinesis in the movies.
I ignore it, and grip the knife harder.
